chief_complaint: Advanced chronic kidney disease (stage 4) with pending kidney transplantation and multiple cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 91‑year‑old woman with a long‑standing history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, obesity, and metabolic syndrome that have progressed to diabetic kidney disease now classified as CKD stage 4 (eGFR likely <30 mL/min/1.73 m²). She has been on the kidney transplant waiting list since March 2019. Cardiovascular disease is extensive, with a prior coronary artery bypass graft (2008) and ongoing ischemic heart disease treated with nitroglycerin, clopidogrel, a beta‑blocker, and antihypertensive therapy. Diabetes management includes insulin and metformin despite advanced renal impairment; the most recent A1c is 3.1 %, suggesting possible overtreatment. She also has anemia of chronic disease, osteoporosis, non‑proliferative diabetic retinopathy, and proteinuria. Psychosocial stressors include recent full‑time employment, chronic stress, intimate‑partner abuse, a criminal record, and limited education, all of which may affect medication adherence and functional status. Dental health is poor with recent loss of teeth. Overall trajectory shows progressive renal decline, high cardiovascular risk, and polypharmacy concerns.
